story.iWant: MCP tools for all user operations
story.soThat: I can help admins manage users conversationally
story.tasks:
- [ ] **T1 – Implement MCP user tools** - [ ] Create `src/mcp/tools/users.ts` with Zod schemas for input validation. - [ ] Implement `list_users` tool: call `UserService.list/search`, return users array. - [ ] Implement `get_user` tool: call `UserService.get`, return single user. - [ ] Implement `create_user` tool: call `UserService.create`, return created user. - [ ] Implement `update_user` tool: call `UserService.update`, return updated user. - [ ] Implement `delete_user` tool: call `UserService.delete`, confirm deletion. - [ ] Implement `reset_user_password` tool: call `UserService.resetPassword`, confirm reset. - [ ] Implement `get_user_credentials` tool: call `UserService.getCredentials`, return credentials array. - [ ] Implement `delete_user_credential` tool: call `UserService.deleteCredential`, confirm deletion.
- [ ] **T2 – Register tools and integrate with MCP server** - [ ] Create `src/mcp/tools/index.ts` to export a `registerUserTools(server, userService)` function. - [ ] Update `src/mcp/index.ts` to obtain `UserService` via `getUserService()` and register tools on startup. - [ ] Ensure MCP server validates connection before registering tools.
- [ ] **T3 – Tests** - [ ] Add Vitest tests for MCP user tools verifying input validation and response structure. - [ ] Verify error responses include IdentiKeyError codes and actionable messages. - [ ] Test tool registration succeeds with mocked UserService.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **MCP tool surface** - Given MCP server is running When tools are listed Then the following user tools are available:
| Tool | Maps to | Input Schema | | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | `list_users` | UserService.list | `{ search?: string, max?: number, offset?: number }` | | `get_user` | UserService.get | `{ id: string }` | | `create_user` | UserService.create | `{ username, email?, firstName?, lastName?, enabled? }` | | `update_user` | UserService.update | `{ id, username?, email?, firstName?, lastName?, enabled? }` | | `delete_user` | UserService.delete | `{ id }` | | `reset_user_password` | UserService.resetPassword | `{ id, password, temporary? }` | | `get_user_credentials` | UserService.getCredentials | `{ id }` | | `delete_user_credential` | UserService.deleteCredential | `{ id, credentialId }` |
2. **Tool metadata** - Each tool has a descriptive `title` and `description` for AI discoverability.
3. **Structured responses (FR50)** - Responses include `structuredContent` with typed data for AI reasoning.
4. **Error handling (FR51)** - Error responses include actionable messages with context (user ID, operation attempted, error code).

doc.title: keycloak-commander — Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet:
As an **AI agent**, I want **MCP tools for all user operations**, So that **I can help admins manage users conversationally**.
Tools: - list_users, get_user, create_user, update_user, delete_user, reset_user_password, get_user_credentials, delete_user_credential.
All tools map directly to UserService methods and expose structured responses for AI reasoning.

doc.title: Architecture — keycloak-commander
Story 2.1: UserService Core Operations
doc.snippet:
UserService is implemented in src/lib/keycloak/services/users.ts with methods covering FR5–FR13, and getUserService() provides a shared factory that MCP and CLI layers consume.
All user-related errors are surfaced as IdentiKeyError with stable ErrorCodes, and tests demonstrate mocking patterns for the Keycloak admin client.

artifact.reason: Backing implementation for all user operations exposed via MCP tools.
Factory that MCP server uses to construct UserService with an authenticated Keycloak client.
Defines the domain types used in MCP schemas for user-related tools.
Defines the MCP tools that wrap UserService methods for listing, retrieving, creating, updating, and managing user credentials.
Exports registration helpers (including user tools) that MCP server startup calls.
Initializes the MCP server, obtains UserService, validates connection, and registers user tools.
Vitest coverage ensuring input schemas, structured responses, and error handling for user MCP tools behave as specified.

story-context.constraints: - MCP tools must remain thin wrappers over UserService and must not contain business logic beyond validation, formatting, and error framing. - All user tools must use snake_case names and follow consistent input/output schema conventions to keep the MCP surface predictable for AI agents. - Tools must return both human-readable text content and machine-friendly structuredContent, with no raw Keycloak representations leaking through. - Error handling must rely on IdentiKeyError and ErrorCodes from the service layer; tools should not invent their own error codes or messages, only format them.
story-context.interfaces:
- MCP user tools: - `list_users(input: { search?: string; max?: number; offset?: number })` - `get_user(input: { id: string })` - `create_user(input: { username: string; email?: string; firstName?: string; lastName?: string; enabled?: boolean })` - `update_user(input: { id: string; username?: string; email?: string; firstName?: string; lastName?: string; enabled?: boolean })` - `delete_user(input: { id: string })` - `reset_user_password(input: { id: string; password: string; temporary?: boolean })` - `get_user_credentials(input: { id: string })` - `delete_user_credential(input: { id: string; credentialId: string })`
Each tool: - Accepts validated input via Zod schema. - Delegates to the corresponding UserService method. - Returns structuredContent shaped around IdentiKey User or credential types.

tests.standards: Use Vitest to test MCP tools with a mocked UserService, focusing on: - Input validation behavior for each tool. - Correct mapping of UserService results into structuredContent. - Error framing that surfaces IdentiKeyError codes and contextual info appropriate for AI debugging.
tests.ideas: - Confirm that list_users passes search/max/offset through to UserService.list and returns a structured users array. - Simulate USER_NOT_FOUND from UserService.get and assert that get_user returns an error payload with the correct code and user id in context. - Validate that create_user and update_user reject invalid inputs at the schema level before hitting UserService. - Ensure that credential-related tools (get_user_credentials, delete_user_credential) return and accept the right identifiers and that errors remain actionable.
